plannedVideo: How can each of four dice have another die that is more likely to beat it?
coldViewerPull: The viewer can choose first, inspect the numbers, and still face a reply with better odds. They want to know where the advantage comes from when the rolls themselves are fair.
expectedPayoff: Winning more often is a relationship between two distributions, not a single strength number. The same four dice form a circular chain of two-thirds advantages; choosing second permits a favorable reply, while any individual roll can still lose.

truthEvidenceStatus.framing: A special set of four equally likely-face dice has a circular chain of pairwise winning advantages. With higher number winning, each possible first selection admits a reply with2/3 win probability. This is mathematical feasibility, not guaranteed victory or physical dice testing.
caveats: Special face labels, not ordinary 1–6 dice; fair means each face is equally likely.
Two-thirds is a one-roll probability under independent equal-face rolls, not guaranteed victory or exactly six wins out of nine.
Use the four-die set as inspected; do not silently turn it into a three-die set or sum-of-two-rolls game.
Source face arrangements and illustrative probability visuals need full claim/visual-truth review after approval; no physical dice, sample game or audience testing performed.
Avoid unverified Buffett/Gates anecdote, gambling advice, AI explanation or universal claim that all rankings are circular.
Editorial risk: four identities and repeated numbers can become bookkeeping. Progressive proof must let a viewer explain the cycle without memorizing four tables.

intendedStory: Invite a choice among clearly unusual numbered dice; establish higher-number-wins and equal face chances; reveal a reply; explain one simple pairing; carry those same objects through the remaining pairings; close the circle and return to the original choice. Reveal face distributions progressively; do not turn the sequence into four repeated probability lectures.
whySelected: Select the dice with no best choice for immediate intelligible involvement and a payoff the viewer can reconstruct: fair random rolls can produce circular pairwise advantages. Flytrap supplies equal wonder and richer living texture; Theseus makes identity criteria felt; Apollo supplies stronger human stakes. Dice most tightly couples the opening choice to progressively visible evidence and a portable insight about comparing distributions. This decision would remain at equal research access and production cost. Retained status, library distance, recent domains and renderer convenience provide no advantage; no predictable virality or brand-new-to-the-world claim.
materialRisks: Do not promise certain wins or conceal unusual face labels.
The main editorial risk is four-die bookkeeping: later development must make the proof visible and progressively comprehensible; production polish alone cannot rescue that failure.
decision: APPROVE PREMISE, REJECT PREMISE with reason, or REVISE PREMISE / FRAMING with specific feedback. Approval permits further research/development only; no claims, script, master or release approved.
